questions.question: 1. In C programming, Arr[1] refers to which element of an array Arr.

explanations.a: Incorrect. This would be true only if array indexing started from 1, which it doesn't in C programming.
explanations.b: Correct. In C programming, arrays use zero-based indexing, so Arr[1] refers to the second element of the array.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Arr[1] refers to a much earlier element in the array sequence.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This would be the first element, which is accessed using Arr[0].

questions.question: 2. The first element of an array is referred to by which index?

explanations.a: Incorrect. While some programming languages use 1-based indexing, C uses zero-based indexing.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Index 2 refers to the third element of the array.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Index 3 refers to the fourth element of the array.
explanations.d: Correct. In C programming, array indexing starts from 0, so the first element is always accessed using index 0.

questions.question: 3. The index of the last element of an array of size n elements is:

explanations.a: Incorrect. Using index n would result in an out-of-bounds error as it exceeds the valid index range.
explanations.b: Correct. Since arrays use zero-based indexing (starting from 0), an array of size n has indices from 0 to n-1, making n-1 the last valid index.
explanations.c: Incorrect. This index is beyond the array bounds and would cause an error.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This would be the second-to-last element, not the last element.
